editorial:
Imagine a giant tower with hundreds of floors, and a single platform of food that slowly drops from the top. The people on the upper floors eat like kings, while those below get nothing but scraps and leftovers. You follow a man named Goreng who wakes up on one of these floors with no memory of how he got there. He shares his cell with a strange older man, and together they try to figure out how this twisted system works. The vibe is dark, tense, and deeply unsettling, but it pulls you in right away. It feels like a nightmare you cannot wake up from, and every scene makes you wonder what you would do in their place.

The acting is strong, especially the lead who carries the whole story on his shoulders. The pacing is tight and never drags, keeping you on edge the whole time. The biggest pro is how the movie makes you think about greed and fairness without ever feeling preachy. The con is that it gets pretty intense and violent, so it is not for everyone. If you enjoy dark thrillers that mess with your head, this is for you.
endingExplained: In the final act, Goreng and his cellmate decide to send a message to the people above by riding the platform down with a single panna cotta dessert untouched. The idea is that if the top floor sees a perfect dish come back up, they will know someone survived below and the system is broken. Goreng stays behind as his cellmate rides up. The last scene shows Goreng alone on a lower floor, possibly dying, while a young girl appears. It is left unclear if the message worked or if the whole thing was just a dream. The twist is that hope itself may be the real trap.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark thrillers and mind-bending stories.
